question_text: A jeweller measured the volume and mass of some samples of silver. He suspects that one of the samples might be fake. The results are listed in the table: Sample: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L; Volume ($x\text{ cm}^3$): 3, 6, 4, 7, 16, 8, 5, 12, 9, 6, 10, 11; Mass ($y\text{ g}$): 40, 95, 50, 160, 285, 130, 65, 210, 155, 90, 170, 190.

subparts.stem: Draw a scatter diagram for this data.

mark_breakdown.desc: Accurate scatter plot of volume versus mass

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A scatter plot plots independent variable $x$ (Volume) against dependent variable $y$ (Mass).
step_by_step: Set up horizontal axis for Volume from 0 to 18 and vertical axis for Mass from 0 to 360.

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct value of r rounded to 3 significant figures

subparts.solution: From linear regression calculation on all 12 points: $r \approx 0.98019806$. So, $r \approx 0.980$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Compute the correlation coefficient $r$ including all data points using linear regression.
step_by_step: Input the 12 pairs of data into the calculator.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding errors or prematurely excluding the suspected outlier.

subparts.stem: Describe the relationship which appears to exist between the volume and mass of the samples of silver.
subparts.solution: There appears to be a strong, positive correlation between the volume of a sample of silver and its mass.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Values of $r$ close to 1 indicate a strong positive linear relationship.

subparts.stem: Do you agree with the jeweller that there is a fake sample?

mark_breakdown.desc: Identifying outlier sample D and concluding agreement with the jeweller

subparts.solution: The data point $(7, 160)$ which corresponds to sample D appears to be an outlier. We therefore agree with the jeweller that there is a fake sample.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: An outlier is a data point that deviates significantly from the overall pattern of the rest of the data.
step_by_step: Examine the scatter plot to find which point lies away from the trend line.
Identify $(7, 160)$ as lying substantially higher than expected for volume 7.
Conclude sample D is the fake sample.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Identifying the wrong point or failing to state agreement with the jeweller.

subparts.stem: Remove the suspect value from the data and find the equation of the regression line for the remaining data.

mark_breakdown.desc: Recalculating linear regression without outlier D

subparts.solution: Using technology with sample D removed: $a \approx 19.4604$, $b \approx -24.6763$. The regression line is $y \approx 19.5x - 24.7$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Removing an outlier provides a more accurate least-squares regression line for the genuine data.
step_by_step: Remove sample D $(7, 160)$ from the dataset.
Compute the linear regression equation using the remaining 11 data points.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Keeping the outlier in the data list while calculating part e.

subparts.stem: Use your equation to find the expected mass of the sample of silver with the same volume as the suspect sample.

mark_breakdown.desc: Substituting x = 7 into the updated regression line

subparts.solution: When $x = 7$, $y \approx 19.5(7) - 24.7 = 136.5 - 24.7 = 111.8 \approx 112$. So, a sample of silver with volume $7\text{ cm}^3$ would weigh approximately $112\text{ g}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Substitute the given value of $x$ into the regression model to estimate the corresponding $y$.
step_by_step: Round to an appropriate integer: $112\text{ g}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the original regression equation with the outlier included.
